correctness.rationale: For 1<p<∞ define level means A_k(f) and scalar ces_p. Scalar norm of L^n follows by telescoping y_j partial sums U_j^p, yielding weighted positive tails H_p(j+1)/H_p(n+j+1); strict log-convexity from positive integral moments makes ratios strictly decreasing, so sharp extremizer is e_n. Level-balanced descendant weights telescope and yield A_k(Bγ^nf)<=|γ|^n A_{k+n}(f), with equality at root for aligned level-n input; this proves the norm and extremizers on every finite-branching tree without assuming regularity. H_p(n+1) asymptotics yield polynomial factor and spectral radius. At |γ|>=1 a finitely supported right inverse S yields mixing; for |>1 summable right inverse satisfies frequent-hypercyclicity criterion and periodic point density. At |=1 positive-density visits to a root target force nonsummable Cesàro level averages, ruling out frequent hypercyclicity, while a periodic point forces a subsequence with uniformly positive level means, likewise contradiction. Independently recomputed infinite zeta-tail norm ratios at p=2 and n=1,2,3,5 with exact equality on e_n and strict inequality for a mixed finite vector. Infinite claims rely on analytic argument, not tests.
